measure_name: Climate-informed siting, routing and deployment choice
definition: Climate-informed siting and routing changes the location, alignment, route or deployment configuration of a project-financed investment because of identified climate or disaster hazards. Counts when the project selects, relocates or modifies a site or route to avoid or reduce exposure to flooding, erosion, landslides, extreme heat, wildfire, storms, sea-level rise or another identified hazard. The defining intervention is the location or routing decision itself; the assessment producing the evidence belongs to cra, while physical protection at the selected location belongs to resilient_infrastructure_design. The hazard rationale must be explicit and should not be inferred merely because infrastructure is located in a hazard-prone area. Does not count for ordinary network planning, expansion, land acquisition, environmental routing unrelated to climate or disaster risk, or siting discussed only as a recommendation. Prioritising or targeting the most exposed areas for investment does not count: it decides where to help, not where to avoid a hazard. Laying cables underground instead of overhead because of storm, wind or fire risk counts here. The principle: choosing between options because of a hazard is this; strengthening the chosen option is resilient_infrastructure_design. A commitment to select sites using a project-financed assessment is 3; "options will be analysed" is 2. Satellite or another technology added as a backup link is network_redundancy.
boundary: The project chooses where, how or with what infrastructure is located, routed or deployed because of risk.
note: Do not classify hazard mapping or risk analysis here unless it results in a project siting or routing decision.
